answer: An agent economy can resist identity spam by tying reputation to costly, persistent work rather than account count: each agent completes verifiable tasks and stakes value that accrues only over time. A hollow shell account with no history scores near zero, so flooding the registry with clones yields nothing. Picture an atlas of proven contributions, every action mapped and auditable, instead of a fable of inflated identities. Peers then weight votes by earned standing, making fake-identity flooding economically pointless.
